subject: Human-Computer Interaction 2
title: Summative Exam: DOM, Web APIs & Client-Side Development

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the relationship between HTML and the DOM?
options: HTML and the DOM are the same thing
HTML is the browser's live object model; the DOM is the static source code
HTML is static markup text; the DOM is the browser's live in-memory object representation
The DOM is generated by CSS, not HTML

questions.text: What does document.querySelector(".btn") return if there are three elements with class "btn" on the page?
options: An HTMLCollection containing all three elements
A NodeList containing all three elements
Only the first matching element in document order

questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an HTMLCollection from a NodeList?
options: HTMLCollection has built-in forEach; NodeList does not
HTMLCollection contains any node type; NodeList contains only elements
HTMLCollection contains only element nodes; NodeList can contain any node type
Both are always static and never update

questions.text: A developer uses document.getElementsByClassName("item") to get a collection, then removes an element from the DOM inside a for loop. What unexpected behavior may occur?
options: The loop throws a TypeError immediately
The collection becomes null after the first removal
Elements may be skipped because the live collection's indices shift as items are removed
Nothing — live collections are immune to mid-loop changes

questions.text: Which property should you use to select the direct parent element of a given DOM node?
What is the key difference between element.children and element.childNodes?
options: children returns a NodeList; childNodes returns an HTMLCollection
children returns only HTML element children; childNodes includes text and comment nodes
childNodes returns only elements; children includes all node types
There is no difference — they are aliases

questions.text: What is the correct 3-step workflow for adding a new element to the DOM using JavaScript?
Which of the following is a key benefit of using addEventListener() over inline onclick attributes?
options: It only works on window objects
It allows multiple handlers of the same type on one element

questions.text: In the syntax element.addEventListener(type, listener, useCapture), what does the optional useCapture parameter specify?
options: Whether the event should be dispatched synchronously
Whether to use event bubbling (false) or capturing (true)

questions.text: What is the primary advantage of using event delegation in JavaScript?
options: It allows a single parent listener to handle events from dynamically added child elements
It eliminates the need for event objects
It automatically stops all default behaviors

questions.text: Which three characteristics define a software widget?
Which Web Sensor API would you use to automatically switch between light and dark UI themes based on the room's brightness?
Why do browsers require explicit Permission Policies before granting access to Web Sensor APIs?
options: To protect user privacy from sensitive data like movement and location
To prevent websites from using too much CPU

questions.text: In the QRious library, what does the level: 'H' option provide?
options: High error correction (up to 30% damage resilience)

questions.text: What type of data does the QRious .toDataURL() method return?
options: An HTML element containing the QR code
A JSON object with QR code metadata
A binary file that must be saved to disk

questions.text: What happens when a long-running synchronous operation executes in a browser's JavaScript environment?
options: It runs in a separate thread automatically
The entire page UI freezes until the operation completes
It is automatically converted to an asynchronous operation
The browser immediately shows a warning

questions.text: In the fetch() API, what is the correct way to handle HTTP error status codes like 404 or 500?
options: The fetch() Promise automatically rejects on 404/500, so catch() handles it
Check response.ok and throw manually if it is false
Use a try-catch block around the entire fetch call
404/500 responses are automatically retried by fetch()

questions.text: What is the correct sequence of steps when processing a fetch() response?
What security requirement must be met for navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia() to function?
options: The page must be served over HTTPS or localhost
The user must have a premium browser
The page must be served over HTTP only

questions.text: Which client-side storage mechanism persists data even after the browser is closed and reopened, and is shared across all tabs from the same origin?
What happens if you store a JavaScript object directly in localStorage without using JSON.stringify()?
options: The object is stored correctly as a reference
The object is automatically stringified by the browser
The value stored is '[object Object]' which is unusable

questions.text: Which cookie security flag prevents client-side JavaScript from reading the cookie's value via document.cookie?
Which attack vector does the SameSite cookie flag primarily protect against?
The HTML DOM is part of the W3C DOM Standard and defines HTML elements as objects with properties, methods, and events.
NodeList returned by querySelectorAll() is always live and updates when the DOM changes.
An anonymous function passed to addEventListener() can be removed later using removeEventListener() with the same function definition.
The fetch() Promise automatically rejects when an endpoint returns a 404 Not Found HTTP status.
The DOM property that moves one level UP the tree to the element's direct parent is _________.
The method used to convert an HTMLCollection or NodeList into a true JavaScript Array, enabling methods like .filter() and .map(), is _________.
The client-side storage mechanism that is automatically cleared when the browser tab or session is closed is called _________.
